newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada housing starts seen raching 132,700 in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada housing starts seen raching 132,700 in 1997.

text.p: Canadian housing starts will rise to 132,700 units in 1997 from a projected 123,000 units this year, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation said on Tuesday.

The government agency said in its third quarter national housing outlook that starts of single detached units will rise 23 percent to 79,100 this year while starts of multiple units will decline by six percent to 43,900.
"The current recovery rests on affordability and tighter supply," said Gilles Proulx, chief economist at the CMHC market analysis center.
He said resale market trends should also remain favorable, due to the recent declines in mortgage interest rates.
